Using the spin tool for creating arches.

content: Make a column, and finish by insetting the top face (Image 1).

image.caption: Image 1 - Making a column for the arch

content: The Spin tool extrudes (or duplicates it if the selection is manifold) the selected elements, rotating around a specific point and axis.

Use the tool to create the sort of objects that you would produce on a lathe (this tool is often called "lathe" tool or "sweep" tool in the literature, for this reason). In fact, it does a sort of circular extrusion of your selected elements, centered on the 3D cursor, and around the axis perpendicular to the working view...
The point of view will determine around which axis the extrusion spins...
The position of the 3D cursor will be the center of the rotation.
Specifies how many copies will be extruded along the "sweep".
When enabled, will keep the original selected elements as separated islands in the mesh (i.e. unlinked to the result of the spin extrusion).
Specifies the axis to use as the pivot of the spin operation.

In Edit Mode, select the inset face. Click the Spin tool on the right (Image 2). We want the spin to go 90° around the y-axis (Image 3). But this doesn't look right. The Spin Tool uses the 3D cursor for the center of the rotation. To fix this, undo the last action, and revert to the Box Select tool. In Object mode, move the column into position where you want the center of rotation to be. In Edit Mode, select the inset face and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D cursor to the top of the column. Then move your column back to where it was. Now we can do the same spin, with the center of rotation where we need it to be (Image 4). Add a Mirror Modifier to finish it off.

image.caption: Image 2 - Bringing up the Spin Tool
Image 3 - Doing a bad spin with the center of rotation in the wrong spot
Image 4 - Adding two more loop cuts

key_concepts: Becoming familiar with several Blender techniques.
Easy and simple beginner exercises to help you understand the different ways of modelling shapes.

content: [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cube to the scene. In Object Mode, check the box for [k]Options > Affect only Origins[/k], and then [k]G,Z[/k] to move the cube's origin to its bottom. Turn this off and [k]G,Z[/k] to move the cube to the origin.
[k]S[/k] until the cube has the dimensions you want (75cm H X 74cm W X 118cm L).

[k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View. [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a loop cut in the middle along the x- and y-axes. Delete the vertices in three of the four quadrants. [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode and add a Mirror Modifier.

[k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, [k]Alt-Z[/k] to turn on X-Ray Mode, [k]1[/k] for Vertex Mode, and grab the vertices at the bottom and move them up to set the thickness of the table top (Image 1).

[k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View, [k]3[/k] into Face Mode and select the top face. [k]H[/k] to hide it. [k]Numpad9[/k] to go into the opposite view. [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add two horizontal and two vertical loop cuts. Move these into position to mark the border under the table and where the legs will come out (Image 2). [k]3[/k] into Face Mode, [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View, and extrude the faces down. Select the face for the leg and extrude it all the way down to the floor (Image 3). [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a Loop Cut to the leg and slide it towards the bottom. Select the edge facing the center of the table and [k]G,X[/k] to move it out, narrowing the bottom of the leg (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 2 - Making edge loops for the border underneath and legs

content: [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cube to the scene. In Object Mode, check the box for [k]Options > Affect only Origins[/k], and then [k]G,Z[/k] to move the cube's origin to its bottom. Turn this off and [k]G,Z[/k] to move the cube to the origin.
[k]S[/k] until the cube has the dimensions you want (90cm H X 42cm W X 49cm L).

[k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View. [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a loop cut in the middle along the y-axis. Delete the vertices in left half. [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode and add a Mirror Modifier.

[k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, [k]Alt-Z[/k] to turn on X-Ray Mode, [k]1[/k] for Vertex Mode, and grab the vertices at the bottom and move them up to set the height of the seat (Image 1).
Follow the same general steps as above to shape the chair. Nothing complicated.

Put your reference images in place. [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cylinder with 16 vertices to the scene. Move it into place above the origin. Scale it down to the correct height, and flatten it to the right height for the bottom. Extrude the top face out and scale it outwards. Do this several times as you go up to create the curve for the bowl. When you reach the top, if you want to round out the edges, [k]Ctrl-B[/k] at the edges to add a curve.

Put your reference images in place. [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cylinder with 16 vertices to the scene. Move it into place above the origin. Scale it down to the correct height, and flatten it to the right height for the bottom. Extrude up to create the shape. If you want to round out the edges, [k]Ctrl-B[/k] at the edges to add a curve.

This will cover the outside. Turn on [k]Viewport Overlays > Face Orientation[/k] to check how it looks. If the top was open, you should see there are no faces inside. You can either close the top with [k]F[/k] in Edit Mode, or add a Solidify Modifier (this will increase the triangle count).

Put your reference images in place. [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cube to the scene. Move it into place above the origin. Scale it down to the correct height. At this point, re-size your reference images to the correct sizes. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, [k]3[/k] for Vertex Mode and [k]A[/k] to select all vertices. [l]M,C[/k] to merge all vertices at the 3D cursor.

In Front View, [k]E[/k] to begin extruding vertices out to match the general profile of the jar (Image 1). Add a Screw Modifier (Image 2). 16 steps is a good number to ensure a round appearance, and if the normals need to be flipped, check the box for [k]Normals > Calculate Order[/k] in the modifier panel. Finally, you can select the vertices at the curve points anf [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to add a bevel to them to round it out (Image 3).

Put your reference images in place. [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cylinder to the scene. You can go with 16 vertices for a decent low-poly model, or 8 vertices for a cartoonish low-poly feel. Go into Edit Mode, select the top face and [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale it in in the x- and y-axes. [k]I[/k] to inset the top face to create the rim, and [k]E[/k] to extrude it down to the bottom to create the inner part of the mug. [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale the bottom face out to match the angle of the mug. Feel free to [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel the edges at the top and inside the mug.
[k]Ctrl-K[/k] to add four horizontal loop cuts around the mug. These will be used for the bands around the top and bottom, and to start the handle. [k]G,G[/k] to slide them into position.
For the bands, [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them and then [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude those faces out along normals. With the outer face selected, [k]S,Z[/k] to scale them.

[url]Get Good at Blender Low poly Metal Structures^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WeFPZAU-gXU[/url]
Make a metal support structure for a wasteland scene.

content: Go to [k]Edit > Preferences[/k] and search for the Auto Mirror tool and enable it. To use the Auto Mirror tool, [k]N[/k] and go to the Edit tab. Go under Auto Mirror. Make sure Apply Mirror isn't checked. Click the button for the axis you want to apply the mirror, and then press AutoMirror. This will add a mirror in the selected axis as well as applying cuts.

[k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cube to the scene. Using the Auto Mirror tool, add mirroring in the x-, y-, and z-axes (Image 1). We don't want three mirror modifiers applied, so after the cuts are made, delete the two additional modifiers and apply the y- and z-axes modifiers to the first one. [k]3[/k] into Face Mode and delete the faces on the sides (Image 2). [k]Numpad3[/k] into Side View, and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add two loop cuts and move them 0.2m from the edge (Image 3). Add a second set of loop cuts 0.15m from the first set (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 4 - Adding two more loop cuts

content: Select the inner faces and delete them. [k]1[/k] into Vertex Mode and select vertices in the upper right corner and [k]F[/k] to fill them in (Image 5). [k]2[/k] into Edge Mode, select the edge at the corner and [k]E[/k] to extrude it to the center (Image 6). Add a Loop Cut down that middle face and then extrude the center vertex down to the center of the structure (Image 7). Make sure clipping is on in your Mirror Modifier.

image.caption: Image 5 - Removing faces and closing off the corner
Image 7 - Adding topology to extrude all the way into the center

content: In Vertex Mode, select the top-right vertex. [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D cursor to the selection (Image 8). Turn off clipping on the modifier. Select all vertices and [k]Shift-D,R,Z,-90[/k] to make a copy and rotate it to the adjacent side (Image 9). Check the normals and [k]Alt-N,F[/k] to flip them if needed. FInally, [k]A,M,B[/k] to remove any extra vertices.

image.caption: Image 8 - Moving the 3D cursor to a selected vertex
Image 9 - Duplicating the topology for the adjacent side

content: In Object Mode, add a Solidify Modifier. Make sure to check the box for Even Thickness.
